Intermediate Throw Event

General Concept: An Intermediate Throw Event in BPMN is used to throw a specific event (message, signal, escalation, etc.) during process execution. It can be used to trigger actions or communicate with other processes or systems.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, Intermediate Throw Events can trigger outbound actions (message, error, escalation, etc.). Output mappings using FEEL expressions can be used to prepare event data. The engine supports error, escalation, and message throw events for advanced process control.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
An Intermediate Throw Event in TaktX allows you to:

  • Trigger outbound actions (message, error, escalation, signal, etc.) during process execution.
  • Define output mappings using FEEL expressions to prepare event data.
  • Control process flow, interruption, or notification based on event type.
  • Configure error handling and compensation for advanced process control.
  • Monitor event creation and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Use for in-process notifications or control flow changes.

 

Example: System Notification with Message Intermediate Throw Event

 

This example shows a process where an Intermediate Throw Event sends a notification (Message Intermediate Throw Event) to another system before continuing. This demonstrates in-process outbound integration in TaktX.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use FEEL expressions to prepare event data.
  • Configure throw event type to match business requirements.
  • Document expected triggers and outcomes.

Pitfalls:

  • Unconfigured throw events may not trigger required actions.
  • Missing output mappings can cause data loss.
